growth_story.headline: Bangladesh grew fast for two decades on garment exports, but income per person growth has slowed each year since 2021 amid unrest and banking stress.
growth_story.arc: From 1990 to 2004, income per person in Bangladesh grew 2.9 percent a year, as the country opened to trade and foreign investment and garment exports took off. From 2005 to 2025 growth stepped up to 5.1 percent a year, and income per person reached its highest level yet in 2025. A World Bank study finds the step-up after 2005 owed less to new reforms than to earlier gains and a stable economy, and the IMF credits growth driven by the garment industry with more jobs and less poverty. Growth stayed between 4.1 and 7.0 percent a year from 2005 to 2019, dipped to 2.6 in 2020 with the pandemic, and recovered to 6.1 in 2021. Since then it has slowed each year, to 2.2 in 2025, and the IMF, World Bank and ADB point to the 2024 uprising, tight policies, banking stress, energy shortages and weak investment.

threads.title: Garments, trade and women's work
threads.text: Garment exports were the engine. A World Bank study finds that more openness to trade and foreign investment supported growth from the late 1990s, and the IMF notes that the garment factories drew millions of young women into paid work.

threads.title: A step-up that held
threads.text: The faster growth after 2005 is harder to explain than the gains before it. A World Bank study finds it did not come from new reforms; instead, earlier gains and a stable economy kept growth from fading, as it usually does in fast-growing countries.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe a slowdown since 2023, with rising poverty and stalled job creation. The averages in the data hide most of it: growth over 2016–2025 averaged 5.0 percent, close to the 5.2 of 2006–2015, and income per person was at its highest level yet in 2025. Only the yearly figures show the slowdown, with growth falling from 6.0 in 2022 to 2.2 in 2025. The level is still rising, but more slowly, and the World Bank says poverty went up even so.
